usageNotes: Use this to migrate an LXC rootfs or mount-point volume to a different storage pool (e.g., local-lvm to ceph), or to reassign a volume from one container to another. The operation returns a task UPID and runs asynchronously — poll the task status before assuming completion. Without `delete: true`, the source volume is retained as an `unusedN` entry in the container config and will consume storage until manually removed.

examples.summary: Move rootfs of LXC 201 from local storage to ceph-rbd, deleting the original

tips: The container does not need to be stopped for a mount-point (mp*) move, but moving rootfs on a running container may fail or require a shutdown depending on storage type.
When moving a volume to a different container (target-vmid), both the source and target containers must be on the same node; use target-volume to control which config key it lands on.
Supply `digest` (from the current container config) and `target-digest` when scripting to guard against concurrent config changes.
Omitting `storage` while supplying `target-vmid` reassigns the volume to the target container on the same storage — useful for splitting a cloned container's disks.
